acceptance.expected: Independent repository handles and OS processes preserve unique identities, stale object/schema/project/endpoint guards, atomic rollback, ordered immutable history and usable recovery across concurrent native/schema/link/resource operations. Every acknowledged update survives; contention may reject explicitly without silent replay.

Identical and conflicting command IDs under genuine process overlap produce at most one durable success per family/identity with exact original intent/outcome inspection after reopen; native plus receipt changes never publish partially.

Declared read-only operations observe one committed native/evidence snapshot without reserving the writer slot. Readers coexist with readers and an active writer under WAL; writes through a read-only transaction reject atomically. Separate requests retain their existing pagination guarantees, without an invented shared snapshot; guarded continuations reject changes as already promised.

Genuinely concurrent assessment and verification work preserves pinned models, selected configuration comparison and candidate applicability. Unrelated head changes never silently change fixed pair meaning; conflicting basis, actions or conclusions reject or require deliberate reassessment.

Process termination before commit leaves no partial native/evidence/outcome writes; termination after commit and response loss recovers exact original success by inspection after restart. No automatic uncertain-write replay.

SQLite-aware online backup during active work restores a complete committed state with native/evidence history and outcome identities intact; current engineering application capabilities remain usable after restore.

Reproducible real-project and connected synthetic workloads report exact candidate, environment, counts, latency distributions, RSS/heap, payload/work bounds and contention. Explicit engineering budgets are fixed after initial baseline and before optimization; overflow is explained, never silently truncated.

Core, typed HTTP/client, CLI and relevant existing shared-workspace task checks cover success, rejection and uncertain recovery under declared workloads. Portable contracts distinguish adapter obligations from SQLite implementation proof; future authentication/backend parity stays unproven.

Appropriate unchanged regression, browser, architecture and quality checks pass. Owning docs, checkpoint, guarded register, deterministic export and restored online backup retain exact evidence, limits and independent delivery/verification/human-validation status. Audit all criteria and the complete goal before completion.

procedure.overlap: Use child-process ready/start/held/release IPC barriers, bounded timeouts and guaranteed cleanup; distinguish separate handles from separate processes. Record actual held lock/snapshot and outcome, not Promise.all alone.
procedure.budgets: Collect initial real and synthetic baselines first. Publish explicit local engineering budgets and sampling plan in a separate immutable budget record before performance edits; no arbitrary-scale claims or retroactively relaxed gates.
procedure.recovery: Terminate disposable workers before/after commit; inspect durable outcomes and full state/history before any deliberate new command. Back up using node:sqlite online API, never main-file copy while active.
procedure.preservation: Live project is backed up before register changes. All adversarial writes use disposable databases or online copies; evidence reports are frozen once observed.

initialAudit.finding: Existing portable concurrency cases serialize through one repository instance. Independent-process read/read probe rejects busy because every SQLite transaction uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE; no lost update established by this probe.

probe.procedure: Independent process holds a repository transaction after a native head read; already-open parent repository attempts a public schema read. No writes occur inside held transaction.

result.message: Database is busy; retry the complete command

probe.interpretation: BEGIN IMMEDIATE reserves the SQLite writer slot for all reads. This probe tests read/read contention, not lost updates or authenticated team behavior.
